description.p: VirtConvert&Create converts virtual disks between VirtualBox, Hyper-V, VMware and QEMU/KVM, and creates new ones: empty, with a formatted partition ready to use, or as a copy of a physical disk. It also writes virtual disks onto physical ones, so a computer starts from them.

ul.li: Writes VDI, VMDK, VHD, VHDX, QCOW2, QED, OVA appliances and raw images; also reads Parallels, DMG and ISO
Hyper-V checkpoints (.avhdx, .avhd) and VirtualBox snapshots are merged with their parents into one disk
Opens the disks inside OVA appliances, and packs disks into OVA files for Import Appliance
New disks of any size with a GPT or MBR partition formatted as NTFS, exFAT, FAT32, ext4, Btrfs or XFS
Copies of physical disks, USB sticks and memory cards, to run in a virtual machine, or of just some of their partitions
Writes any virtual disk onto a USB stick, memory card, SSD or hard disk, fitted to its size and read back to check it
Every copy can be compared with its source, byte for byte, before it is saved
Shows whether the disk boots with UEFI or BIOS, and what to set in VirtualBox or Hyper-V
Converts several images in one go; a command-line interface for scripts

description.p: A tidier main window: the toolbar keeps the everyday actions, the image is summed up in two lines, the options moved into Convert to, the activity log folds away (and opens by itself when something goes wrong), and tips are behind Details.

ul.li: Write virtual disks onto physical disks (Write to disk; virtconvert write): every format, checkpoints merged, read back and compared, the partition table fitted to the disk
Long file names wrap in the Image box instead of widening it
Create new disks: empty, partitioned, or formatted with NTFS, exFAT, FAT32, ext4, Btrfs or XFS
Copy physical disks into virtual disks
New formats: QCOW2, QED, OVA and raw are written; Parallels, DMG, ISO, QCOW and OVF are read
VMDK as one file, preallocated with a -flat file, or in 2 GB files
